skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for signs of blunt aortic injury or mediastinal pathology.
steps: Assess the width of the superior mediastinum relative to the thoracic diameter (widening is typically >8 cm or >25% of thoracic width at the level of the aortic knob).
Inspect the costophrenic angles and lung bases for the 'deep sulcus sign' (an abnormally deep, lucent costophrenic angle) which indicates a subpulmonary pneumothorax.
Distinguish blunt aortic injury from isolated pneumothorax by confirming the presence of mediastinal widening alongside basal lucency, rather than tracheal deviation or normal mediastinal contours.
